# A nonuniform target envelope in one continuous dimension

This lemma does not resolve the higher-dimensional conjecture. It separates
the existence of an arbitrary target law from the false uniform-target claim.

Let S have finitely many positive interval fibers I_z=[l_z,u_z], with ordinary
one-dimensional volume in each fiber, total mass M, and normalized measure mu.
Assume these fibers are induced by a convex body. Let the integer marginal be
eta, and let z0 be a positive fiber whose marginal halfspace depth is beta>0.
Thus every closed halfspace in the integer-coordinate space containing z0 has
eta-mass at least beta. Integer coordinates may have any dimension n.

For t in R put

  L(t)=inf_a mu{x<=t+a dot(z-z0)},
  R(t)=inf_b mu{x>=t+b dot(z-z0)},

where a,b range over R^n. Both functions are Lipschitz, with constant at most
N/M when N fibers are nonempty: changing t by Delta changes every interval
cap length by at most |Delta|, uniformly over its slope. L is nondecreasing,
and R is nonincreasing.

For every t,

  L(t)+R(t)>=beta.                                      (1)

Indeed, the two caps with slopes a,b cover every entire fiber with
(a-b) dot(z-z0)>=0. If a=b, they cover all fibers. Otherwise the indicated
integer halfspace has marginal mass at least beta. The sum of the two cap
masses is therefore at least beta. Taking independent infima over a and b
proves (1); attainment of either infimum is unnecessary.

At the endpoints of I_z0=[l,u], one has L(l)=0 and R(u)=0. For an elementary
justification, replace the inducing body by the convex hull of all its
interval fibers; this leaves every integer fiber unchanged. The resulting
set is a polytope with finitely many interval endpoints. Its lower and upper
fiber functions on the projection admit affine supports at z0, relative to
the affine hull of the integer support. Extending these affine functions
to R^n gives lower and upper supporting graphs. Their through-endpoint caps
have zero interval volume. This also handles integer support on a proper
affine subspace.

Define

  F(t)=min{L(t)/beta,1}.

Together with F=0 to the left of l and F=1 to the right of u, this is a
continuous nondecreasing cumulative distribution function: the endpoint
claims and (1) give F(l)=0 and F(u)=1. Its probability measure nu is supported
in the one selected fiber and is nonatomic. For every closed ambient
halfspace H,

  nu(H)<=mu(H)/beta.                                    (2)

For a nonvertical left halfspace, its restriction to the selected fiber is
(-infinity,t], whose nu-mass is F(t)<=L(t)/beta. Its original mu-mass is at
least L(t). For a right halfspace, (1) gives
1-F(t)<=R(t)/beta. The absence of atoms includes boundary equality. For a
vertical halfspace containing z0, marginal depth gives mu(H)>=beta and
nu(H)=1; if it excludes z0, nu(H)=0. This proves (2) for all orientations.

Any median of nu is a single deterministic point of S. Every containing
halfspace has nu-mass at least 1/2, hence mu-mass at least beta/2. In
particular, weighted Doignon supplies beta>=2^(-n), yielding exactly the
requested continuous-dimension-one constant.

The density of this envelope measure has not been shown log-concave. In
higher continuous dimensions, independently constructed one-dimensional
envelopes in different directions need not be the projections of one common
measure. That compatibility is not assumed here.
